preconditions.description: The input string `str` must be a non-empty digit string of length between 1 and 30, representing a positive integer (no leading zeros).
The integer `k` must be between 1 and 10, representing the maximum allowed number of swap operations.

postconditions.expression: all(c in '0123456789' for c in return_value) and len(return_value) == len(str)
postconditions.description: The output `return_value` must be a string of the same length as `str`, composed exclusively of digits.

postconditions.expression: return_value == ''.join(sorted(str, reverse=True)) or (k == 0 and return_value == str)
postconditions.description: If `k` is 0, the output must be identical to `str`. Otherwise, the output must be the lexicographically largest possible string obtainable by performing at most `k` swap operations on the digits of `str`.

postconditions.expression: all(return_value[i] >= str[i] for i in range(len(str))) or (k == 0 and return_value == str)
postconditions.description: For each digit position `i`, the output digit must be at least as large as the corresponding digit in `str`, unless no swaps are allowed (`k == 0`).

postconditions.expression: any(return_value[i] > str[i] for i in range(len(str))) or (k == 0 and return_value == str)
postconditions.description: If `k > 0`, the output must be strictly larger than `str` in at least one digit position (lexicographical order), or identical to `str` if no swaps are allowed (`k == 0`).
